labels.label: T-abs-rational-line-extras/1-time-function
labels.notes: The constants were read off the elaborated type (Expr.getUsedConstants). rationalLine_hasTimeFunction states Causal.Causality.HasTimeFunction rationalLine, which is the ladder's `lean` for time_function (programme/ladder.toml:255), and Iff.rfl with it. #print gives HasTimeFunction C := exists T, Continuous T and (forall x y, C.le top x y -> x != y -> T x < T y). The proof takes T = id; strictness comes from rationalLine_le_real (x <=_U y gives x <= y in R). rationalLine_curvesExtend states Causality.CurvesExtend (ladder.toml:261) and follows through HasTimeFunction.curvesExtend. The statement is closed, with no hypothesis. True: on the rational line, x <=_M y with x != y is the branch x < y.

labels.label: T-abs-rational-line-extras/2-strongly-causal-open
labels.notes: rationalLine_stronglyCausalOpen states Causality.StronglyCausalOpen (ladder.toml:182). #print gives: forall p, forall U in nhds p, exists V : Opens, p in V and V subset U and C.CausallyConvexIn V top. CausallyConvexIn V U means V subset U and the full diamond diamond U p q lies in V for p, q in V, which is defi:convexite_causale (ETT.tex:657-660) read in M. The witness is the open interval (l, u), convex because rationalLine_diamond_subset_Icc gives J_U(a, b) inside [a, b] for every open U. StronglyCausal (ladder.toml:176) follows by StronglyCausalOpen.stronglyCausal. Both statements are closed.

labels.label: T-abs-rational-line-extras/3-not-locally-causally-open-future
labels.notes: rationalLine_not_locallyCausallyOpenFuture is the negation of Causality.LocallyCausallyOpenFuture (ladder.toml:283). #print gives: forall x, exists W, x in W and CausallyOpenFutureOn W, i.e. J+_U(V) is open for all opens V <= U <= W. causal_ladder proves it from h, together with rationalLine_absolutelyMinimal as a `have`. The rule it uses is AbsolutelyMinimal.causallyOpenFuture_of_locallyCausallyOpenFuture (Causal/LadderLocal.lean:264, attribute in Causal/Ladder/Rules.lean:44). The contradiction is rationalLine_not_causallyOpenFuture (Causal/NestedConverse.lean:373). The two-sided form, rationalLine_not_locallyCausallyOpen, is the negation of Causality.LocallyCausallyOpen (ladder.toml:290). #print gives the future form for C and for C.dual. It is proved by causal_ladder through locally_causally_open => locally_causally_open_future. Both statements are closed.

labels.label: T-abs-rational-line-extras/4-not-tarentin
labels.notes: rationalLine_not_tarentin is the negation of Causality.Tarentin (ladder.toml:240). #print gives: forall x, forall U in nhds x, exists p in U, exists q in U, x in openDiamond top p q. This is def:tarentin_spacetime (ETT.tex:677-680, quoted verbatim in the docstring). It is proved through rationalLine_openDiamond (U p q : any), which says that interior (diamond U p q) is empty, for every open U and not only top. The argument: an interval around x holds irrationals v < x < w. p <=_U v and p <=_U w force p = v = w (rationalLine_eq_of_le_irrational). The closer's finding on roadmap.toml:810 is true. I proved it in a probe, then deleted it: rationalLine.diamond top p p = {p} for irrational p, so the claim that every J_top(p, q) lies in Q fails (sqrt 2); every J_top(p, q) lies in Q union {p}. The conclusion is unaffected.

labels.label: T-abs-rational-line-extras/5-not-causally-plain
labels.notes: rationalLine_not_causallyPlain is the negation of Causality.CausallyPlain (ladder.toml:234). #print gives: forall U (A : Set M), interior (Jplus U A) subset closure (Iplus U A), and the same with minus. The Lean quantifies over every A, while defi:causalement_plat (ETT.tex:283-287) asks A subset U. The negation is witnessed at U = top and A = univ, which is inside U, so the paper's form fails too: J+_M(R) = R and I+_M(R) is empty.

labels.label: T-abs-rational-line-extras/6-no-chronal-neighbours
labels.notes: rationalLine_not_chronalNeighbours is the negation of Causality.ChronalNeighbours (ladder.toml:299). #print gives ChronalPastNeighbours C and ChronalPastNeighbours C.dual, where ChronalPastNeighbours: forall V, forall v in V, exists p in V, C.lt V p v. The rational line's lt is False, so the past side fails at V = top, v = 0. The alternatives the REPORT cites exist at the stated lines: ChronalNeighbours.tarentin (Causal/ChronalTarentin.lean:179) and PushUp.causallyPlain_of_chronalNeighbours (Causal/CausallyPlainLocZ.lean:202).

labels.label: T-abs-rational-line-extras/7-not-causally-compact
labels.notes: rationalLine_not_causallyCompact is the negation of Causality.CausallyCompact (ladder.toml:198). #print gives: forall p q, IsCompact (diamond top p q). This is def:causally_compact (ETT.tex:350-352, quoted verbatim). rationalLine_diamond_top (p q : Q) gives diamond top p q = range Rat.cast inter Icc p q. The mathematics checks: for rational p, p <=_top x iff x is rational and p <= x, and likewise at q. Then J(0, 1) is not closed, since an irrational in (0, 1) is in its closure. The SCOPE discloses that the formula is for rationals only; with an irrational endpoint the diamond is {p} (if p = q) or empty, which I checked. The target title's unqualified 'J(p, q) = Q inter [p, q]' is read correctly as the rational case. rationalLine_not_globallyHyperbolic follows by GloballyHyperbolic.causallyCompact.

labels.label: T-abs-rational-line-extras/8-separation
labels.notes: I printed the elaborated type of rationalLine_separates. It has 18 conjuncts: AbsolutelyMinimal (the constant is Causal.Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimal, the ladder's lean for absolutely_minimal, ladder.toml:222), IsCausal, PushUp, LocallyPushUp, HasTimeFunction, CurvesExtend, StronglyCausalOpen, StronglyCausal, and the negations of CausallyArcConnected, CausallyOpenFuture, CausallyOpen, LocallyCausallyOpenFuture, LocallyCausallyOpen, Tarentin, CausallyPlain, ChronalNeighbours, CausallyCompact and GloballyHyperbolic. This is exactly the REPORT's list (labels[7].hypotheses[0]). It contains every conjunct of rationalLine_separates_absolutelyMinimal (NestedConverse.lean:394). Every for_keeper `from` id (the eight positives) and every `to` id (the six new entries and the three re-pointed ones) is a conjunct. rationalLine_absolutelyMinimalOn (W : Opens R) states Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimalOn rationalLine W for every W. #print gives: for every S covering W and every open V <= W, every le_V (resp. lt_V) is a TransGen of le (resp. lt) in V inf O, O in S. So its universal closure is 'absolutely minimal on every open set for every cover of it', as claimed. It has the same form as halfLightLine_absolutelyMinimalOn (Causal/Dec8MinimalWitness.lean:165), which kb/0074 and OQ-69 (registers/DECISIONS.md:225) call the gluing reading of defi:causalite 'as OQ-18 describes it'. OQ-18 (DECISIONS.md:174) itself says only 'absolute minimality'. The universal form implies that one at W = top (Precausality.absolutelyMinimal_iff), so the 'either reading' claim holds under both phrasings.

findings.what: The proposed README row says 'not causally compact (`J(p, q) = ℚ ∩ [p, q]`)' without qualification. As stated this is false for irrational endpoints: with p irrational and q > p rational, J(p, q) is empty while ℚ ∩ [p, q] is not. This is the same kind of imprecision the closer reported in roadmap.toml:810. The Lean (rationalLine_diamond_top, p q : ℚ), the module docstring and the SCOPE all qualify it correctly.
findings.fix: Write '`J(p, q) = ℚ ∩ [p, q]` for rationals `p`, `q`' (or '`J(0, 1) = ℚ ∩ [0, 1]` is not closed') when the master adds the row.
